newsitem.title: CHILE: Codelco hopes to end Davila futures probe by June.
newsitem.headline: Codelco hopes to end Davila futures probe by June.

text.p: Chile's state copper giant Codelco expects to wrap up its three-year investigation into failed futures trades by former operator Juan Pablo Davila by mid-year, said a top official.
"All in all we shouldn't go beyond June, except as far as the cases before the courts continue," Juan Eduardo Herrera, Codelco's senior sales vice president, told Reuters.
Codelco has started lawsuits in London against Belgium's Sogemin Ltd and German trader Metallgesellschaft in connection with Davila's bad deals which cost the corporation $175 million in 1993.
Codelco has accused the firms of paying secret kickbacks to the high-flying trader who was fired as soon as the losses were uncovered in early 1994.
Asked if Codelco planned legal action against another trader Merrill Lynch, Herrera replied: "If we had found evidence of wrong-doing, we would have presented a claim."
But he added, "We are still working on Merrill Lynch. We have not finished yet."
Herrera said Codelco has helped Chilean judge Jose Benquis in his investigation into allegations Davila carried out deals for Minera El Bronce while he was working for the state firm.
El Bronce is owned by relatives of ex-Codelco president Alejandro Noemi.
"We have helped Benquis, but we don't have much information on that company (El Bronce)," he said.
He declined to comment on the results of Codelco's own enquiries into the El Bronce trades.
Benquis is waiting for a report from Britain on the deals before deciding whether to close his case, or to continue the probe. He has said he hopes to end his enquiries this month.
Once he wraps up his investigations, Benquis must rule on charges against Davila including fraud and carrying out business "incompatible" with his position in Codelco.
Metallgesellschaft and Sogemin are accused of paying millions of dollars into bank accounts belonging to Davila and his associates in the Cayman Islands. Both have denied any wrong-doing.
The scandal over the losses stained the reputation of Codelco, the world's largest copper producer, and shocked international metals markets from London to Hong Kong. Noemi resigned in disgrace.
Davila was released from preventative custody in a Santiago jail last year to undergo cancer treatment.
